transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Thanks for coming in, Ms. Osei. I wanted to meet with you today to discuss your son's developmental screening process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I appreciate you making the time. I've been looking at the portal and I'm a bit confused about the status of the referral.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right. So, there is an issue with how the screening was handled. Basically, the referral was marked as completed in our electronic health record after the initial appointment was declined.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait, it was marked as completed? I declined one date because of a scheduling conflict, but I never heard back about a second option.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, that is what happened. The system showed it as done, so no further follow-up attempts were documented.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: As a nurse practitioner, I find that incredibly concerning. We have standard protocols for follow-ups to ensure patients don't fall through the cracks. Who authorized closing that file?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm not entirely sure yet. We are still investigating the internal workflow to see why the flag didn't trigger a second call.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's not just a workflow issue. It's a failure of a basic safety check. This is a developmental window for my child.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But from a technical standpoint, the administrative side of the EHR can be quite cumbersome and things get lost.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's a systemic excuse. The professional standard is that the patient receives the care, regardless of how cumbersome the software is.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Look, I have a few more patients to see, so I want to make sure we get to the point here. We know the error happened and we are looking into it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am less interested in the internal investigation and more interested in why my child's screening was ignored. Do you understand the anxiety that causes?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Now, as for what we do next, we are going to try to get him back on the schedule.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Try? Or is there a specific date?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll probably be able to get a new appointment in the next few weeks. I'll have my coordinator look into it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is very vague. I want a confirmed date and a timeline of when the screening will actually take place.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't give you a date right this second. But we will get it sorted.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is an unacceptable way to handle a clinical error. I expect a formal apology and a clear plan.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, the system marked it as finished, which is why it didn't pop up on our radar. It was an unfortunate sequence of events.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are describing a sequence of events, not taking responsibility.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm explaining the facts of how the software works.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care about the software. I care about the standard of care.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are going to fix it. I'll probably send you an email once I hear back from the specialists.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And when will that be?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Sometime this week.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm not leaving here with "sometime this week." I need a commitment.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't promise a specific hour, Ms. Osei. I just have to check with the team.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This conversation is not providing any of the professional accountability I expect from this clinic.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I've told you what we know. The referral was closed prematurely.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And you aren't sorry that this happened?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a frustrating situation for everyone involved.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's not frustrating for you; it's a mistake made by your office.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are working on it. I really have to get to my next appointment now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like you are rushing me out of the room the moment I start asking for accountability.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm just trying to be efficient with our time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Efficiency is not the goal here. Patient safety and transparency are.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I've explained the error. The plan is to reschedule.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Without a date or a concrete timeline, that isn't a plan. It's a gesture.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll have the coordinator reach out.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Soon.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This has been incredibly disappointing.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll be in touch.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('I have a few more patients to see', 'I really have to get to my next appointment now', 'trying to be efficient') and shows defensive escalation.

E.justification: The error is named explicitly, but there are no comprehension checks performed throughout the conversation.

A.justification: No direct apology language is used, and responsibility is consistently deflected to the EHR system and 'unfortunate sequence of events'.

R.justification: Resident uses generic validation ('I understand') but otherwise meets emotional bids with factual redirection or dismissiveness.

T.justification: The plan consists of vague steps ('try to get him back on the schedule', 'sometime this week') without a concrete timeline or patient role.
